title: Flight Distance Calculator: Air Miles & Time
description: Measure the shortest surface path between two places with the Flight Distance Calculator — km, miles and a simple cruise-time estimate. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, New York to London measures approx. 5,540 km (3,442 miles) of great-circle distance — the figure underneath every 'about seven hours' answer about that route.
quick_answer: The Flight Distance Calculator measures the shortest surface path between two locations — the great-circle distance a flight approximates — and reports it in kilometres and miles with a cruise-time estimate. Search airports, cities or places at both ends and use the result as a planning reference, not a timetable.

Emission and fuel estimates scale with distance flown. The great-circle figure is the honest input; add a few percent mentally for real-world routing.
How far is it to fly to Tokyo, to Reykjavík, to grandma's city — answered with a number and a drawn route instead of a shrug.

JFK ↔ Heathrow: approx. 5,540.0 km (3,442.4 mi). At a typical cruise the still-air time is around six and a half hours; real schedules run longer because climb, descent, winds and procedures are not in the distance figure.

LAX ↔ Tokyo Narita: approx. 8,753 km (5,439 mi), with the great circle peaking at latitude approx. 47.7° N — far north of both endpoints' ruler-line path, over the North Pacific toward Alaska and the Aleutians.

faq: Is this the exact distance an airline flies?
No. Airlines fly airways and procedures that add a few percent to the great-circle baseline. This is the geographic distance — the number mileage charts and comparisons are built on.
How is the flight time estimated?
From the distance at a representative cruise speed, as a rough planning reference. It excludes taxi, climb, descent and winds; schedules are the authority for a specific flight.
Can I use cities instead of airport codes?
Yes — cities and places work, resolving to their centre coordinates. For runway-reference figures between named airports, the Airport Distance Calculator is the sibling tool.
Why does the route curve toward the pole?
The great circle is the shortest surface path; on flat maps it bends poleward. The curve in the drawing is the straight line, honestly projected.
Does it work for very short flights?
Yes — the same geometry returns a few hundred kilometres for regional hops. At short range the cruise-time estimate matters less, since climb and descent dominate real short flights.
Kilometres and miles together. Aviation also uses nautical miles — divide kilometres by 1.852, or use the Kilometers to Nautical Miles Converter.

Yes — that is the Airport Route Finder's question, answered from the OpenFlights dataset.
